short: Genghis Khan's successor, under whom the empire reached the Danube and acquired an administration.
full:
Ögedei was elected khagan at a kurultai on the Kherlen in September 1229, two years after his father's death, having been named as heir over his elder brothers. He was reckoned the most conciliatory of them, and the choice held. Under him the Jin dynasty of northern China was finished off in 1234, campaigns opened against the Song, Korea was subdued, and Batu and Subutai carried the western army through Rus' into Poland and Hungary.

He also gave the conquests a machine to run on. He built a walled capital at Karakorum, extended the yam relay system across the empire, imposed regular taxes in place of ad hoc plunder, and employed the Khitan minister Yelü Chucai, who argued successfully that taxed peasants were worth more than emptied provinces. Ögedei drank heavily and died on 11 December 1241, days after a night of it. His death recalled the armies from Europe and began a five-year interregnum under his widow Töregene.
